title: Empanadas
subtitle: baked pastry parcels with spiced beef filling
excerpt: Flaky hand-made pastry parcels filled with spiced beef, pepper, and olive. They are baked, not fried, which makes them lighter. This recipe makes 12 and they disappear fast.
sourceNotes: Empanadas are eaten across Latin America and Spain. The Argentinian version, particularly from the provinces of Salta and Jujuy, is considered some of the finest. Each region has its own fillings and fold.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze unbaked on a tray, then transfer to a bag. Bake from frozen at 200C for 30 minutes.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make and shape the day before. Refrigerate and bake the next day.

content.text: Keep the pastry dough cool and do not overwork it. Rest it in the fridge before rolling. Seal the edges firmly -- any gap means the filling will leak during baking.

items.prepNote: 1 for the dough, 1 for egg wash

content.text: Make the pastry: rub the cold butter into the flour until it resembles breadcrumbs. Add 1 egg, salt, and 3 to 4 tbsp cold water. Mix to a smooth dough. Wrap and rest in the fridge for 30 minutes.
Make the filling: fry the onion and pepper in oil for 5 minutes. Add the beef mince and cook until browned. Add the spices, olives, and season well. Cool completely.
Preheat oven to 200C (fan 180C / gas 6). Line two baking sheets with baking paper.
Divide the dough into 12 balls. Roll each into a 12cm circle on a lightly floured surface.
Place a spoonful of cold filling onto one half of each circle. Fold the other half over. Press the edges firmly and crimp with a fork or twist-fold to seal.
Place on the baking sheets. Brush with the beaten egg.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until golden brown.

items.cause: Dough too warm or not rested
items.fix: Keep the dough cold. Rest it for at least 30 minutes. If it tears, press the edges together and work quickly.
Press the edges very firmly after folding. Dampening the edge with water before sealing helps it stick.

items.cause: Mince overcooked or not enough fat
items.fix: Do not overcook the filling. A small knob of butter stirred in while still warm adds moisture.

content.text: Empanadas are found across Latin America, Spain, and the Philippines. Argentina is famous for its version. The filling and the fold vary by region and by town. They are eaten at street markets, family gatherings, and every occasion in between.
